ga_easy_crack_area_2.blurb: A small granite bouldering zone inside the Boat Rock field on the west side of Atlanta, holding about a dozen problems. Grades run from V0 up to a single V8, but the bulk sit between V0 and V2, so it suits newer boulderers and warm-ups well. Many visitors begin their day here before moving on to the harder sectors. The setting is a slabby, sharp-grained boulder field, with a tall slab wall running beneath the boulders, so a crash pad and a spotter are worth bringing. Expect a short stroll from the parking lot and plenty of company on busy weekends.

ga_croc_boulder_the.blurb: A single large sandstone block at Rocktown, the well-known boulder field near LaFayette in northwest Georgia, carrying eleven problems. The attraction is a tall, steep face on the far side of the block, tucked out of view from the main path, so you need to circle around to find it. Difficulty is concentrated in the middle, mostly V3 to V5, with a few harder lines up to V8 and a lone V2. Expect powerful moves on an overhanging wall and a high topout. Bring several pads and spotters, as the landings and height call for care.

ga_main_wall.blurb: The principal wall on the left side of the Turtle cliff in northeast Georgia, offering twelve traditional routes. Grades start around 5.6 and reach 5.11, with the heaviest cluster at 5.9 and 5.10, so it rewards climbers comfortable placing their own gear on moderate to hard lines. Turtle as a whole is quiet, rugged and not set up for beginners or large groups. You can get to the foot of the wall on a trail or drop in from above by rappel. Expect little traffic and a committed, backcountry feel.
